name: CTAL — Continuous Trust and Assurance Ledger
one_line_value_proposition: A fail-closed gate that releases a protected action only when content and license checks both pass, and records every decision in a signed, offline-verifiable ledger.
buyer_problem: Teams that release AI-generated or licensed content must show why each release was allowed. Logs held in the operator's own database are weak evidence: whoever controls the database controls the record.
solution_summary_public: CTAL runs AQPD (content acceptability) and CLES (license entitlement) as separate checks, combines them with a fail-closed decision matrix, signs the result as an Ed25519 assurance envelope, and appends it to a tenant-scoped, hash-chained ledger. A signed export can be verified offline with a pinned key.
differentiators_public: Two independent checks combined by an exhaustively tested fail-closed matrix (49 combinations; only ACCEPT + AUTHORIZED proceeds by default).
Offline verifier states what it did and did not establish, rather than only returning pass/fail.
Tenant isolation, idempotent retries, key rotation/revocation and reversible migrations are implemented and tested.
verified_capabilities: Fail-closed orchestration verified for timeout, exception, invalid result and signing failure (tests: test_gate).
Signed assurance envelope; any field change, addition, removal or key/algorithm swap fails verification (test_envelope).
Tenant-scoped hash-chained ledger with tamper detection for edit, delete, reorder, substitute and truncate (test_ledger, test_export).
Signed export and standalone offline verifier with pinned trust root (test_export; `python3 -m ctal demo`).
License activation limits, live per-tenant revocation, incident-to-regression replay, metrics, TLS and rate limiting (test_online).
92 tests pass locally (pytest, Python 3.13, 2026-10-15); GitHub Actions workflow 'ctal' succeeded on main at 934c993 (Python 3.9 and 3.12).
unverified_claims: Production AQPD detection accuracy: the AQPD engine is a deliberately simple reference engine and makes no accuracy claim.
Behavior under production load or multi-node deployment (SQLite single-writer).

public.headline: Prove every AI release decision — and let your auditor verify it without trusting your database.
public.subheadline: CTAL gates a protected action behind two independent checks (content acceptability and license entitlement), signs each decision, and exports an evidence package that an independent offline program can verify.
public.cost_of_inaction: Release decisions that cannot be independently evidenced are hard to defend in an audit or dispute. This is a qualitative risk statement; no market statistic is cited.
public_limitations: AQPD and CLES here are reference implementations; the production engines were not supplied. Optional adapters run externally supplied JS engines; crypto.js is a labelled reconstruction.
A hash chain alone does not stop a database administrator who rewrites history and recomputes hashes; customers must retain earlier signed exports.
The export signing key is the offline trust root; its holder can sign a forged export.
architecture_public: Request → AQPD check + CLES check → fail-closed decision matrix → signed assurance envelope → tenant-scoped hash-chained ledger → signed export → offline verifier.
Python 3.9+ with the `cryptography` library; optional Node 22 bridge for externally supplied JS engines.
public.risk_summary: Reference-grade AQPD/CLES engines (no accuracy claim); single-node SQLite; ownership and AI-authorship review pending; no revenue or customers.

demo.title: Run the end-to-end CTAL demonstration
steps: The demo creates a temporary ledger with development keys and synthetic content.
It gates content under six AQPD/CLES combinations.
It exports a signed evidence package and verifies it offline (exit 0).
It tampers with one envelope and shows the verifier fail (exit 1).
demo.limitations: Development keys and synthetic data only. Recorded output of a real run; not a hosted service.

diligence_preview: Tests: Tested implementation: 92 passing tests and green CI. Not verified in production use.
Dependencies: Python `cryptography` (Ed25519) plus the standard library; optional Node 22 for the JS adapter. Full dependency and license inventory is provided in the private diligence package.
Security posture: automated secret and pattern scan only; no manual security review yet.

Known limitations: AQPD and CLES here are reference implementations; the production engines were not supplied. Optional adapters run externally supplied JS engines; crypto.js is a labelled reconstruction. A hash chain alone does not stop a database administrator who rewrites history and recomputes hashes; customers must retain earlier signed exports. The export signing key is the offline trust root; its holder can sign a forged export. Single-node SQLite; no HA.
